summary: Hermes parallelism layer — ACTIVATED (v1.3, 2026-06-12, T001-T015). Within-plan DAG concurrency: generate-workstreams.py assigns parallel_group=level-{depth} via assign_ws_depths (longest-path depth); hermes-execute.py runs a level-aware loop: compute_ready_level (deps done) → partition_level (greedy graph-coloring; scope_unknown/serialize_all → singleton sub-batches; HIGH-severity conflicts separated) → asyncio.gather bounded by asyncio.Semaphore(max_parallel_workstreams) held for full run_workstream lifetime. Cross-plan: run_cross_plan(--slugs/--plan-set) calls build_plan_conflict_graph (scope-path intersection or scope_unknown → conflict), acquire_plan_locks (sorted ascending slug order, deadlock-free INV-6), schedule_batches (greedy coloring), asyncio.Semaphore(max_parallel_plans). Single in-process asyncio.Lock serializes all merge_workstream calls. Default caps = 1 (opt-in via HERMES_MAX_PARALLEL / HERMES_MAX_PARALLEL_PLANS; INV-5: cap=1 ≡ legacy sequential). Non-file shared state (DBs, ports) NOT protected — use serialize_all escape hatch.

entry_points.summary: Async coroutine: creates worktree, spawns pi session, polls status, merges. Acquires merge_lock (asyncio.Lock) around merge_workstream call. Semaphore held for full lifetime.
Async: reads workstreams.json for one slug, runs compute_ready_level → partition_level → asyncio.gather loop. Accepts merge_lock from run_cross_plan for cross-plan merge serialization.

Async: multi-slug entry point. Calls build_plan_conflict_graph, acquire_plan_locks, schedule_batches. Creates single in-process asyncio.Lock threaded to all run_single_plan calls. Bounded by asyncio.Semaphore(max_parallel_plans).

Greedy graph-coloring: partitions a ready level into sub-batches where no two workstreams in the same sub-batch share a HIGH-severity file_conflicts edge (when serialize_high_severity=True). scope_unknown or serialize_all → singleton sub-batches.
Returns workstreams whose depends_on are all in terminal_status (done). depends_on is the sole scheduling gate (INV-2).
Builds plan-level conflict graph: two plans conflict iff file-scope path-sets intersect OR either is scope_unknown/low-confidence/missing. Fail-safe: unknown scope always conflicts.
Acquires plan-claim locks in SORTED ascending slug order (INV-6: deadlock-free). Releases all on any failure. Returns held locks.
Greedy batch coloring over the plan conflict graph: disjoint plans grouped in same batch, conflicting plans serialized. Returns ordered list of batches.
Computes longest-path depth for each workstream over the depends_on DAG. Sets parallel_group='level-{depth}'. Same-depth workstreams are mutually independent by construction.

Parses **Files:** lines from each task block in TASKS.md to derive per-workstream file scope. If any task lacks a parseable **Files:** line, scope_unknown=True → conservative full serialization (INV-4).
Synchronous git merge of hermes/<slug>/<ws_id> into base. Called under the in-process asyncio.Lock — never runs concurrently across workstreams or plans.

invariants: INV-1: Concurrent workstreams write to isolated git worktrees; the working tree is never shared.
INV-2: depends_on is the sole scheduling gate — a workstream starts only when all its depends_on IDs reach 'done'. parallel_group is a derived label, NOT a scheduling mechanism.
INV-3: merge_order is authoritative for merge sequence — merges always proceed in declared order, never in completion order.
INV-4: scope_unknown=True or serialize_all=True forces fully-sequential execution (singleton sub-batches). Silent blind parallelism is forbidden when conflict data is absent or low-confidence.
INV-5: max_parallel_workstreams=1 (default) reproduces pre-v1.3 sequential behavior exactly. cap=1 ≡ legacy sequential.
INV-6: Plan-claim locks are always acquired in sorted ascending slug order — prevents AB/BA deadlocks across concurrent super-orchestrators.
INV-7: parallel_group and scope_unknown are additive fields (forward-compatible). Pre-v1.3 manifests omitting scope_unknown default to false; null parallel_group treated as scope_unknown (fail-safe).
gotchas: Semaphore is held for the FULL run_workstream lifetime (spawn → monitor → merge), not just at spawn time. This bounds live sessions, not spawn rate (audit M1).
poll_session runs via asyncio.to_thread so one stalled poll cannot starve sibling coroutines.
GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 is set for the run and restored after — prevents concurrent git gc contention against the shared object store.

Non-file shared state (databases, ports, remote sandboxes, in-memory caches) is NOT protected by the file-conflict layer. Use HERMES_SERIALIZE_ALL=1 to force fully-sequential execution when workstreams share such resources.
scope_unknown is derived from parse_task_files: if ANY task block in TASKS.md lacks a parseable **Files:** line, the entire plan is treated as scope_unknown=True.
The merge_lock is a single in-process asyncio.Lock — it serializes merges across all workstreams AND all plans within one run_cross_plan call. Two plans never merge concurrently.

cap=1 is the safe default — parallelism is opt-in via HERMES_MAX_PARALLEL / HERMES_MAX_PARALLEL_PLANS. Do not raise caps in production without first verifying workstreams have no non-file shared-state dependencies.

config_keys.note: All Hermes concurrency knobs are ENV-ONLY, read by scripts/hermes/config.py ConcurrencyConfig. They map to ConcurrencyConfig fields.

concurrency.description: Max workstreams running concurrently within a single plan. Default 1 = legacy sequential (INV-5). Semaphore held for full workstream lifetime.
Max plans running concurrently in a cross-plan run. Default 1.
Force fully-sequential execution regardless of conflict analysis. Use when workstreams share non-file state (DBs, ports). Equivalent to scope_unknown=True for scheduling.
When True, HIGH-severity file_conflicts edges force serialization within a level even when max_parallel_workstreams > 1.

runbook.non_file_shared_state_note: If workstreams share databases, ports, remote sandboxes, or other process-level resources, set HERMES_SERIALIZE_ALL=1. The file_conflicts layer does not model these dependencies.
